key_insight: Mesoscale neural operators learn nonlocal constitutive laws from molecular dynamics while preserving strain energy density and fracture energy under horizon rescaling.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables continuum fracture simulations on domains far larger than atomistic training specimens while retaining learned nanoscale material behavior.
method: Learn a nonlocal kernel and nonlinear constitutive relation from MD loading and displacement data.
Normalize the kernel to preserve strain energy density as the nonlocal horizon changes.
Rescale critical bond stretch to maintain consistent fracture energy across scales.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests supported model recovery; MD-based tests achieved energy metrics within 3% and out-of-distribution peak forces within 6%, while a plate with 4,000× the training-specimen area exhibited branching fracture.
watch_item: The reported tests do not establish generalization to other materials or fracture regimes, so new applications require validation.
paper_title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
